subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — response cadence and evidence request
body:
From: Alex Reynolds <areynolds@novakon.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novakon.com, cnguyen@novakon.com
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form indemnity — initial ask

Hi Ben / Kimberly,

Thanks for the draft Order Form. Procurement has one sticking point on indemnity: Novakon cannot accept a unilateral limitation that excludes third-party IP claims tied to outputs generated for our account. We need the vendor to defend and indemnify for third-party claims that allege Novakon infringed IP due to using Redwood outputs (including AI-generated content).

Specific asks:
- Confirm Redwood will defend/respond for third-party IP claims where the claim arises from outputs provided to Novakon under the SOW/Order Form.
- Provide proposed language for the Order Form (Section 8 / Indemnity).
- Evidence of mitigation: can you provide a short note on training provenance / filtering processes and a contact for technical evidence if this becomes an issue?

We hope to close legal redlines by end of week to hit procurement timelines.

Regards,
Alex
Alex Reynolds
Head of Procurement, Novakon

---

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alex Reynolds <areynolds@novakon.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — initial ask

Alex — thanks for the clear note.

Quick plan:
1) Legal (Kimberly) to propose compromise language (cap + carveouts + notice/cooperation).
2) Product (Marissa) to provide a short provenance / filtering note for procurement.
3) We can join a 30-min call tomorrow if that helps accelerate.

I've attached our redlines (draft) to show where we can be flexible and where we need a carveout for AI-generated outputs trained on third-party data.

Call availability: Tue 10th 10:00-11:00 PT or Wed 11th 14:00-15:00 PT.

Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: NOVA_MSAs_redlines.pdf (pdf, 42 KB)

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alex Reynolds <areynolds@novakon.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 13:47:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Order Form indemnity — initial ask

Alex (and Ben),

Thanks — appreciate the specificity. I read Novakon's proposed redlines and wanted to offer a compromise that addresses Novakon's exposure while keeping Redwood operationally viable. Below is proposed language for the Order Form (redline-friendly):

"Vendor Indemnity for Third-Party IP Claims. Vendor will defend, at Vendor's expense, and indemnify Customer from and against any third-party claim that the Customer's authorized use of Services and outputs provided by Vendor under this Agreement, when used in accordance with the Documentation and the Order Form, infringes or misappropriates such third party's intellectual property rights; provided that: (a) Customer provides prompt written notice of the claim and reasonable cooperation; (b) Vendor has sole control of the defense and settlement of the claim; and (c) Vendor's liability shall not exceed the greater of (i) USD 3,000,000 or (ii) the total fees paid by Customer to Vendor under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim.

Exclusions: Vendor will have no indemnity obligation for claims arising from (i) Customer content or instructions that materially alter the Services; (ii) Customer's use of outputs outside the scope of the Order Form or documentation; or (iii) Customer's failure to follow Vendor's reasonable mitigation instructions.

This strikes a defend-and-indemnify commitment for covered IP claims while preserving a commercial cap and logical exclusions. If Novakon needs a higher cap, we can discuss escalation to Sales leadership (Ben/Jeremy) and possible insurance-backed approaches.

Regarding evidence: Marissa, could you send a short one-page note describing (i) data sources used for models deployed to customers, (ii) content-filtering and prompt-safety layers, and (iii) contact for technical escalation? Procurement typically wants this to route evidence requests.

Best,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline-summary-kp-v1.docx (docx, 18 KB)

---

From: Alex Reynolds <areynolds@novakon.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: cnguyen@novakon.com, procurement@novakon.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:50:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — initial ask

Kimberly — thanks for the thoughtful counterproposal. Two quick points from our GC: 
1) The cap of $3,000,000 is lower than our internal risk tolerance for strategic customers; we'd expect either a higher cap or a carve-in for IP claims that impact our business directly (we proposed $10M).
2) We want assurance that Vendor will make available technical evidence (logs, model provenance) under NDA and on reasonable notice to support defense.

We are open to the exclusions you listed, but the carveout for "Customer content or instructions that materially alter the Services" needs to be narrowed — our use case is standard prompt-based generation for marketing & product copy; that's within normal use and should not knock us out of coverage.

Would Redwood consider a tiered cap tied to ARR or a carve-in for demonstrated customer impact?

Alex

---

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Reynolds <areynolds@novakon.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order Form indemnity — initial ask — product note

Hi Alex / Kimberly,

Per Kimberly's request, attaching a short note (model-provenance-note.txt) that covers:
- Model lineage: we publish model family and training cutoff dates for each model in the catalog; we do not disclose raw training datasets, but we provide provenance metadata (source types: public web, licensed corpus, synthetic augmentation).
- Filtering & mitigation: customer-facing runtime filters (PII, policy blocks), optional content-safety hooks, and a recommended webhook for evidence collection (prefix/KV cache snapshots + request/response traces) under NDA.
- Evidence process: we will accept formal evidence requests routed to security@redwood.com; typical turnaround 3-5 business days for logs and provenance metadata, longer for deep forensics.

Note on "materially alter": our product team defines "material alteration" as (i) fine-tuning or uploading custom model weights, or (ii) running model-consuming transforms that rewrite or inject third-party content outside normal prompt/response. Simple prompt use and template-based generation do not constitute "material alteration." Happy to add that explicit language.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: model-provenance-note.txt (txt, 4 KB)

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alex Reynolds <areynolds@novakon.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novakon.com, cnguyen@novakon.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Order Form indemnity — response cadence and next steps

Alex — thank you and Carly. Based on internal discussions, our recommended path to close this week: 
1) Redwood proposes final redline for the Order Form with (a) defend-and-indemnify language limited to outputs used in accordance with Documentation, (b) cap at $5,000,000 with an exception allowing escalation to senior execs for strategic customers to reach $10,000,000, and (c) clarified exclusion language that narrows "material alteration" to the two specific product actions Marissa listed.
2) We will provide the model-provenance-note and a named technical contact (security@redwood.com / Sam Park) under NDA for evidence requests.
3) If Novakon needs a different commercial solution (higher cap), Ben will run expedited pricing/insurance options and revert within 24 hours.

If that works, please confirm and we will circulate a tracked redline of the Order Form and a DocuSign link for signature.

Best,
Kimberly
